events.title: T-Mobile’s $85 Billion Debt Load Won’t Feel the Fed’s Rate Hike the Way Wall Street Thinks
events.summary: T-Mobile's substantial debt load is largely insulated from recent Federal Reserve rate hikes because most of its $86.9 billion debt consists of fixed-rate notes, not floating-rate debt. Only about $1 billion of its debt is tied to floating rates, making the common Wall Street calculation of a $212 million increase in annual interest largely misleading. The company's strong free cash flow, projected at $18.4 to $18.8 billion for 2026, further mitigates the impact of any incremental interest costs, positioning T-Mobile more favorably than some analysts suggest.

articles.headline: T-Mobile’s $85 Billion Debt Load Won’t Feel the Fed’s Rate Hike the Way Wall Street Thinks

events.title: Jim Cramer Notes RTX Faces Valuation Pressure as Rates Rise
events.summary: Jim Cramer highlighted that RTX Corporation (NYSE: RTX) is facing valuation pressure due to rising interest rates, which are causing price-to-earnings multiples to shrink. Despite RTX reporting strong Q2 sales and increased EPS guidance, its high valuation could be problematic if earnings growth doesn't offset the declining multiple. The company is also working to address supply chain constraints to convert its substantial backlog into revenue.

articles.headline: Jim Cramer Notes RTX Faces Valuation Pressure as Rates Rise

events.title: Caesars confirms FTC seeks more merger details, two board members step down
events.summary: Caesars Entertainment announced that two board members, Jesse Lynn and Ted Papapostolou, who were appointed at the request of investor Carl Icahn, have resigned. The company also disclosed that both Caesars and Fertitta Entertainment received a second request for information from the FTC regarding their merger, indicating continued regulatory review. events.title: Lockheed Martin gets first batch of Patriot interceptor parts from General Motors
events.summary: Lockheed Martin has received its first shipment of critical Patriot interceptor components from General Motors, less than a month after the two companies signed a manufacturing agreement. This expedited delivery, which traditionally takes months, highlights the Pentagon's push for faster weapons production amid surging global demand for missile defense systems like the Patriot, especially from Ukraine. Lockheed Martin is also significantly investing to scale up its munitions output across several U.S. sites.

articles.headline: Lockheed Martin gets first batch of Patriot interceptor parts from General Motors

events.summary: Uranium Royalty Corp. (NASDAQ: UROY) announced a significant financial upturn, reporting a 1530% increase in net income to $16.3 million for the quarter ending July 31, 2026, with diluted EPS rising 900% to $0.10. events.title: Automaker Stocks Rally as Rotation Lifts Cyclicals: General Motors Climbs 4%, Stellantis Rises 4%, Ford Gains 3%, Tesla Adds 2%
events.summary: Automaker stocks, including General Motors, Stellantis, Ford, and Tesla, all saw significant gains Thursday morning due to a rotation into cyclical stocks, rather than company-specific news. This movement indicates investors are betting on softer interest rates and steadier consumer confidence, driving capital towards vehicle manufacturers. However, this type of rotation-driven bid can be indifferent to individual company performance and may reverse without a fundamental catalyst.

events.title: Atlantic Coca-Cola Bottling Contributed $753 Million to Iowa Economy
events.summary: A new report reveals that Atlantic Coca-Cola Bottling Company significantly boosted Iowa's economy, contributing $753 million in 2025. The company, one of 61 independent bottlers, operates 10 facilities across five states, employs over 800 people, and has invested more than $40 million in modernizing its operations. Nationally, the Coca-Cola system contributed $85 billion to the U.S. economy and supported nearly one million jobs last year.

articles.headline: Atlantic Coca-Cola Bottling Contributed $753 Million to Iowa Economy
